articles.title: Wang Cong says eye poke led to slow start in first statement following main event loss to Natalia Silva at UFC 332
articles.summary: Wang Cong was defeated by Natalia Silva at UFC 332
articles.body:
Wang Cong says an early eye poke led to her not having the performance she wanted in Wang's first ever UFC title fight.

Natalia Silva captured the UFC women's flyweight title with a unanimous decision victory over Wang in the main event of Saturday's UFC 332 event in Salt Lake City. Silva seemed to be cruising to a win, but Wang began to turn things up a notch — especially in the fifth round — but it was too little, too late for the 34-year-old.

In her first statement since the loss, Wang says she was poked in the right eye in the first round, which took her a bit to get through.

"Thank you for supporting, my friends," Wang said on Instagram. "The game is lost. What a pity. I have some regrets then because of the first [round], the eye was poked in the second half. The line of sight is blocked and then I couldn't see it when I was poked in the right eye in the first [round]. Wait until later to slow down, it's too slow to enter.

"Where to fall, get up, go back and summarize yourself. Come on, try again."

Silva and Wang fought for the title that was vacated by Valentina Shevchenko to close out a wild card in the promotion's return to Utah.

articles.title: La UFC anuncia el regreso de Pereira ante Pavlovich y la pelea entre Oliveira y Lopes por el cinturón BMF
articles.standfirst: El UFC 335, última cartelera numerada del año, supondrá la vuelta de 'Poatan' y el supercombate entre Charles Oliveira y Diego Lopes
articles.summary: El UFC 335, última cartelera numerada del año, supondrá la vuelta de 'Poatan' y el supercombate entre Charles Oliveira y Diego Lopes
articles.body: El día de ayer fue histórico para la UFC, ya que el criticado UFC 332 no solo superó las expectativas, sino que se convirtió en la cartelera con más K.O. de la historia de la promotora -11-. Además, durante el evento la compañía anunció los dos combates estelares del UFC 335 que se celebrará el 12 de diciembre en el T-Mobile Arena de Las Vegas, y que supondrá el regreso de Alex Pereira para medirse a Sergei Pavlovich, además de un duelo por el cinturón BMF entre Charles Oliveira y Diego Lopes. De hecho, también se hizo oficial la pelea entre Bo Nickal y Joe Pyfer en peso medio como otro aliciente interesante para la cartelera. El pasado 14 de junio, 'Poatan' se enfrentó a Ciryl Gane por el cinturón interino de peso pesado con el objetivo de ser primer campeón en tres categorías diferentes de la historia de la UFC. Sin embargo, fue noqueado en el intento, y tras saberse la noticia de que Tom Aspinall dejaba vacante el cinturón indiscutido pidió una revancha inmediata contra 'Bon Gamin' al considerar que hizo trampas dándole golpes ilegales en la nuca. Desgraciadamente, la UFC consideró que era mejor enfrentar a Gane contra el polémico Josh Hokit en el UFC 334 que se celebrará en noviembre en el Madison Square Garden. Aun así, Pereira afirmó que su plan era mantenerse en peso pesado y ganarse de nuevo la oportunidad titular, por lo que se enfrentará a Pavlovich en un reto que en caso de superar le volvería a dar la oportunidad de ser triple campeón, esta vez por el cinturón indiscutido. Alex tiene una cita con la historia, aunque tendrá que amoldar su físico para que la subida a peso pesado no le vuelva a pasar factura. La pelea entre Pereira y Pavlovich ni siquiera será el combate estelar, ya que ese protagonismo se lo llevarán Charles Oliveira y Diego Lopes con el cinturón BMF en juego. El pasado marzo 'Do Bronx' le arrebató el título a Max Holloway con una masterclass de grappling, y en su primera defensa dará la bienvenida a peso ligero a su compatriota, que debuta en las 155 libras después de pelear hasta dos veces por el cinturón de peso pluma ante Alexander Volkanovski -perdió ambas por decisión-. Lopes es sinónimo de espectáculo, un peleador de compañía y que tiene todos los atributos necesarios para pelear por un cinturón de este calibre. Además, posee el talento suficiente en el jiu-jitsu para frenar los derribos de 'Do Bronx' y dar un buen show en la pelea en suelo. En principio, Charles se iba a medir a Arman Tsarukyan en el UFC 331, pero el fallecimiento repentino de Allan Nascimento -peleador de la UFC y uno de los mejores amigos de Oliveira- le obligó a tomarse unas semanas de descanso. Por tanto, ha habido cambio de planes y ahora a la última cartelera numerada del año ha reunido a 'Do Bronx' y 'Poatan', dos de las mayores superestrellas de la UFC.

articles.title: Rich Chou Teases Ki MMA’s New Rules as Promotion Looks to Break From UFC Formula
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, Rich Chou hinted that Ki MMA could feature different rules than what fans are accustomed to with the UFC. The post Rich Chou Tease...
articles.body:
Rich Chou hinted that Ki MMA could feature different rules than what fans are accustomed to with the UFC. The new upstart promotion is expected to host its inaugural event in early 2027.

Ki MMA is a new promotion spearheaded by former Bellator and Strikeforce president Scott Coker. Chou joined the promotion in an executive role and is eager to showcase Ki MMA's vision.

Ki MMA will offer a much different viewing experience for fans who may only be familiar with the UFC.

The fights will take place in a ring instead of a cage. There will also be two fights in one night when the promotion crowns its first featherweight World Grand Prix champion.

Rich Chou Hints at New Rules to Break From the UFC Formula

Rich Chou said that there are different ways for an MMA promotion to stand out. Among some of those changes are the rules, which Chou hinted could be different than the UFC.

"You see it with our format, with the Grand Prix global finale having two fights in one night. I think you'll see us, I can't go fully into this, but I'll tease you a little, that we are looking at ways to innovate the rule set. Having an entirely different presentation and format, and style. We're going to really create our own thing, and I think that's very important," Chou exclusively told Heavy Sports via The Game Plan .

Chou also clarified that the promotion will still be abiding by the unified rules of MMA.

"Here in North America, we are limited with creativity because of the unified rules. But we are going to be promoting all over the world, and so we're having discussion about how can we be creative in certain times, moments, and areas, and how that can make fighters and fans more excited, and give them something different," Chou said.

"Fans want to see something different, but also fighters, there are a lot out there and we're having those conversations now, that would love to utilize a different rule set."

Chou Stresses Importance of Successfully Being Different

Chou also stressed the importance of being differently and successfully accomplishing that.

He admitted that while Ki MMA wants to be different from the UFC, they must do so with a lot of thought put into it. However, if Ki MMA tries to be different just for the sake of being different, it will not be successful.

"If you're going to look like them and have the same format, and just be a light version to your point, that's a tough position to be in. That's a tough shadow to get out of no matter who you are and who you have fighting."

"Something I've thought of a lot lately, there have been other MMA promotions out there, and at one point Bellator included, where you kind of say to yourself, 'Well, the goal is to be Pepsi to Coke , right?' I think we've heard that, we've read that. We don't want to be Pepsi to Coke, we don't even want to be a soda. We're a different thing. Call us premium sparkling water or something like that," Chou exclusively told Heavy Sports via The Game Plan .

articles.title: Dana White reveals how Ronda Rousey took only “minutes” to change his NO WOMEN policy in UFC mindset
articles.summary: Dana White has revealed that it took only a few minutes for Ronda Rousey to change his mind about women fighting in the UFC.
articles.body: Dana White has revealed that it took only a few minutes for Ronda Rousey to change his mind about women fighting in the UFC. White had previously insisted that women would “never” compete inside the promotion. However, a brief conversation with Rousey at a UFC event made him reconsider his position.White recalled that Rousey approached him and asked for 15 minutes of his time. They spoke privately at the arena. Within minutes, White said he realised that Rousey had the personality and determination needed to lead a new women’s division. Her success later proved that decision right and helped transform women’s MMA.Ronda Rousey changed Dana White’s view in minutesUFC President Dana White has often spoken about the meeting with Ronda Rousey. It became one of the most important moments in UFC history.“Ronda Rousey grabbed me at an event, said, ‘Hey, I’m Ronda Rousey. Can I get 15 minutes with you?’ We went into my room at the arena… and, I don’t know, minutes into the conversation, I’m like, ‘Holy shit. I think I’m going to do this and she’s the one to do it with,’ you know?” White said.Before their conversation, White had publicly maintained that women would never fight in the UFC. Rousey challenged that view with her confidence and belief in herself.According to White, Rousey stood out from other fighters. She had a strong personality and a clear understanding of how she could become a major star. She also had a huge amount of self-belief.White eventually decided that Rousey could become the face of women’s MMA in the UFC.The decision quickly produced results. Rousey became the UFC’s first female fighter. She was also named the inaugural UFC Women’s Bantamweight Champion.Her performances made her one of the biggest stars in the promotion. Rousey became a major pay-per-view attraction and headlined several UFC events.Her popularity also helped change the UFC’s approach to women’s MMA. More female fighters were given opportunities. Multiple women’s divisions were eventually introduced.The success of Rousey also helped open the door for future stars. Fighters such as Amanda Nunes, Joanna Jędrzejczyk and Cris Cyborg went on to become major names in the sport.White and Rousey have also remained close despite their careers taking different paths. Rousey has described White as one of her closest friends and has credited him with playing an important role in her career.Their relationship continued even after Rousey moved away from the UFC. Before her return to combat sports against Gina Carano at a Most Valuable Promotions event shown live on Netflix, Rousey reportedly gave the UFC an opportunity to make a counter-offer.White instead supported her decision. He also sent Rousey a supportive message on fight day.There has even been speculation about Rousey’s future in MMA leadership. articles.title: Dana White family life: UFC President made his sons do construction work while enjoying UFC success with wife Anne, his relationship with his estranged mother and more
articles.summary: UFC President Dana White has opened up about his approach to family, work and raising his children.
articles.body: UFC President Dana White has opened up about his approach to family, work and raising his children. Despite building one of the biggest combat sports organisations in the world, White says he wanted his sons to understand the value of hard work from an early age.White’s comments come as he has also spoken about his difficult relationship with his late mother, June White. His family life has often been complicated, but White has been clear about one thing. He wants his children to build their own paths and understand the effort required to succeed.Dana White opens up on wanting his sons to understand what real work looks likeDana White and his wife, Anne, have three children. Their sons are Dana White III and Aidan White, while their youngest child is daughter Savannah White.White has previously said that he never wanted to force his career path on his children. He wanted them to find something they genuinely enjoyed. However, he also wanted them to understand the importance of showing up and working hard.That is why White made his sons experience construction and other manual jobs.His view is connected to the way he built his own career. White did not come from a wealthy background. He has often spoken about working hard before becoming one of the most powerful figures in combat sports.White believes that young people can learn valuable lessons by working alongside others.“This younger generation thinks you can work from home and build a successful business. It’s impossible… A lot of good ideas come from everybody being at work”, he said on The Diary of Ace Podcast.For White, the lesson was not simply about earning money. He wanted his children to understand responsibility, discipline and the value of being around other workers.His children have ultimately followed very different paths.Dana White III developed a passion for football. He played the sport at the University of San Diego after growing up playing football in Nevada.Aidan White initially followed his brother’s interest in football. He later moved towards combat sports and made his amateur boxing debut in 2018. He eventually became involved with action sports and Nitrocross through Thrill One.Savannah White has followed a quieter path. She has stayed away from much of the spotlight surrounding her father and brothers.White’s approach to parenting has also been shaped by his own complicated family history.His relationship with his mother, June White, became deeply strained. June wrote an unauthorised 2011 biography about her son, Dana White: King of MMA, which was highly critical of him and his behaviour.White later spoke openly about their falling-out. He said a series of increasingly aggressive emails demanding money contributed to the breakdown of their relationship.June died in 2023. articles.title: Human vs humanoid robot cage fight goes viral
articles.summary: Frankie LaPenna fought three robots in a cage, including two modified EngineAI T800 humanoids that can kick with up to 850 pounds of force..
articles.body: We've watched humanoid robots play soccer, run races and even fight other robots. Now, content creator Frankie LaPenna has taken things in a much wilder direction by stepping into a cage to fight them himself. The event was staged by REK, a robotics entertainment company that puts remotely controlled humanoids into live combat events. In San Francisco, LaPenna faced three robots in a series of bouts, including two full-size EngineAI T800s, as part of what REK billed as the first human-versus-humanoid robot cage fight. The viral footage getting most of the attention comes from one of those T800 fights. LaPenna moves toward the robot and throws several punches. The machine fires back with punches and kicks before one shot sends him flying across the cage. And if the robot looks like it walked straight out of "The Terminator," that was clearly the point. But the bigger story here is what these machines can actually do, who was controlling them and how much of the fighting was really driven by AI. Watch the free replays and get your checklists at CyberGuyLive.com The bigger robots were modified EngineAI T800s After facing a smaller Unitree G1, LaPenna went up against two modified EngineAI T800s, built by Chinese robotics company EngineAI. EngineAI lists the standard T800 at about 5 feet 8 inches tall and roughly 165 to 187 pounds, depending on the version. REK describes the modified machines used in its fights as about 6 feet tall. For the event, REK also gave the T800 a much more intimidating look. The mechanical head and glowing red eyes lean heavily into "The Terminator" theme. Put a machine that size inside a fighting cage and you can see why the video grabbed so much attention. There was a person controlling the robot Here's the big thing to know about this fight: there was a human behind the controls. REK's technology partner Reflex Arc says pilots operate the humanoids in real time using VR gear or a gamepad. AI helps with balance and trained movement, while the human pilot directs the action. So when you see a T800 throw a punch or launch a kick, the robot is carrying out the pilot's commands. It is not independently deciding how to fight LaPenna. That still leaves plenty to be impressed by because the machine has to stay upright, recover from contact and turn those commands into real physical movement inside the cage. HUMANOID ROBOT VIDEOS SHOW MACHINES LASHING OUT Frankie LaPenna actually fought three robots The viral clip getting most of the attention only shows part of what happened that night. According to REK CEO Cix Liv, LaPenna faced three robots during the event. He reportedly started against a smaller Unitree G1 before moving on to two modified EngineAI T800 humanoids. REK says its modified T800 machines can kick with up to 850 pounds of force, which helps explain why the footage looks so intense. LaPenna was knocked down during one of the T800 bouts, but Liv said he recovered, knocked the robot off balance and ultimately ended the fight with the robot's head coming off. REK has continued teasing more footage, and the short clips circulating online still do not show the full sequence of all three bouts. So what most people are seeing online is only one part of the event. The fight took a physical toll on LaPenna The physical side of the fight became pretty clear once LaPenna started trading punches with the robots. Liv said LaPenna originally wanted to fight without protective equipment, but REK insisted that he wear it. He ultimately entered the cage in motorcycle-style protective gear and gloves. According to Liv, LaPenna injured his hand while punching one of the robots but otherwise avoided a serious injury. Even with a human controlling the machine remotely, LaPenna was still trading blows with a heavy metal robot capable of putting real force behind its movements. REK is betting on robot fighting as entertainment REK has been building toward this kind of event for a while. The company stages live fights where people remotely control humanoid robots against other humanoid robots. It also has a simulator that lets players learn the controls before some get the chance to pilot the real machines. Reflex Arc says REK's first simulator championship generated 3,670 matches, with the winners flown to San Francisco to pilot real robots at REK2 in August. The simulator uses the same basic controls and trained balance system as the physical robots. That helps explain where REK is going with all of this. The idea is to take something that feels like a video game and put it into a real fighting cage with actual humanoid robots. Then LaPenna stepped inside and raised the stakes by putting a person on the other side. LET'S LOOK BACK ON THE BEST MOMENTS (READ: CRASHES) FROM THE WORLD HUMANOID ROBOT GAMES We've seen robot fighting before Robot combat itself is nothing new, and we've been following that evolution closely. In 2025, four Unitree G1 humanoids fought in a boxing-style tournament in China. Those machines were also controlled by human operators, and the matches included punches, kicks and knockdowns. We have also watched humanoid robots play soccer without human control, rally on a tennis court and kick soccer balls hard enough to leave visible dents in a wall. REK's event takes that progression in a different direction. This time, the person sharing the cage with the machine can actually feel what happens when that robotic strength comes back at them. What this human vs humanoid robot fight really shows Strip away the Terminator head and the social media theatrics, and there is a pretty remarkable robotics demonstration underneath it. The larger T800s weigh as much as about 187 pounds, yet they can stay balanced in a confined fighting area, absorb contact and execute punches and kicks under human control. The hardware is clearly becoming more capable. Compare today's humanoids with the awkward walking robots we were watching only a few years ago, and the change is dramatic. And something tells me Frankie LaPenna will not be the last person crazy enough to climb into the cage with one. Kurt's key takeaways I've watched humanoid robots do some pretty wild things, but seeing one kick a person across a cage definitely got my attention. The big thing to remember is that there was still a human pilot behind the controls. These robots were not independently deciding how to fight LaPenna. AI helped with balance and trained movement while a person directed the action in real time. What stands out to me is how quickly the physical side of this technology is advancing. These machines can stay upright through contact, recover and put some serious force behind their movements. REK even required LaPenna to wear protective gear before sending him into the cage. It makes for a viral video, but there is a more serious side to this, too. As humanoid robots become stronger and more capable, we are going to have to think carefully about who is controlling them, what safeguards are in place and where this kind of power should be used. articles.title: Ben Whittaker: Conor Wallace scare raises questions over light-heavyweight's title credentials, says Matthew Macklin
articles.summary: Ben Whittaker beat Conor Wallace by unanimous decision in Birmingham on Saturday, despite a wobbly final three rounds for the Olympic silver medallist; Sky Sports' Matthew Macklin says Whittaker needs more fights before his shot at the IBF light-heavyweight belt which the win earned him
articles.body:
After controlling the fight from the start, Whittaker was troubled by a left hand from Wallace in the 10th round and then looked ragged in the 12th as he repeatedly slipped to the canvas before clinging on to claim a points win on Saturday in Birmingham.

Whittaker's victory lined up a shot at the IBF light-heavyweight belt which is held by unified champion Dmitry Bivol, but Macklin believes the Olympic silver medallist is not yet ready to challenge the Russian.

Macklin told Sky Sports : "Ben has been on a run of pretty spectacular performances, hasn't he? That said, if we're honest about the calibre of opposition, we know it's pretty low for him and where he is aiming towards being.

"All of a sudden, they stepped it up again with Conor Wallace. He boxed really well for most of the fight, but nonetheless, at the end of the fight, he struggled.

"He got caught and then struggled to shake off the effects of that shot. He recovered momentarily, but not properly. He got his head together a little bit, but was still hurt because you could see he didn't really regain control of the fight.

"I think he needs more than one [fight before Bivol], probably a few.

"While Conor Wallace is a nice boxer, you wouldn't put him in the category of your Bivols and your Callum Smiths.

"Look at the fight between Callum Smith and Joshua Buatsi, and what those two went through in that fight, and then you see how Whittaker unravelled on Saturday night, there's no way you'd say he beats those two guys.

"He has the skill, the sleekness, the speed and the savvy to mix it with those guys, but has he got the toughness, the chin, the stamina, the power, the hardness to mix it with those guys over 12 hard rounds? He hasn't shown that so far.

"That's not to say that Ben isn't tough or hard. But we can only judge him on what we've seen, and we've seen him unravel a couple of times.

"In the first Liam Cameron fight, he was unravelling and then obviously they both fell out the ring. Fair play to him, in the rematch, he came out and looked brilliant, but against Conor Wallace, he was boxing well, controlling it, but then gets nailed a couple of times and, all of a sudden, he starts to unravel.

"Fair play again, he got through it. But against a Bivol or a Callum Smith, or a Buatsi or William Hutchinson, would he have got through it against those guys? Probably not.

"I think [his trainer] Andy Lee has done a great job with him, but I also think that there's only so much you can do in the gym. You've still got to get the experience on the night, under the lights, in a real fight against real high calibre opposition.

"What's happened with Ben in his career, is he hasn't fought enough high level opposition. If you look at who he has boxed, outside of Cameron and Conor Wallace, he's boxed absolutely nobody.

"For someone who was a top-class amateur, to be a professional as long as he has and to have fought the level of opposition he has, he's missed years of learning - and that could be a problem at the top level.

"It's great getting the highlight-reel knockouts - it's great for your ego, for the perception of you and from a promotional point of view, to create the star quality and the hype. That's important when you're trying to build a star, but you also need to build the fighter.

"You can't just build a star without building a fighter, because at some point he's going to be in a battle against another real fighter, who is of a high level, who wants it as much as he does, and can take a shot and give a shot.

"If you're not getting seasoned, if you're not putting the stuff that you're learning in the gym into practice, on the night and when you need it, it won't be there because you haven't developed it.

"By the way, I like him a lot and I want him to do well, but he hasn't been managed well in his career in terms of the opponents he's fought. He needs some proper fights."

articles.title: Paddy Pimblett propone un The Ultimate Fighter contra Ilia Topuria... y Dana White está a favor
articles.standfirst: El peleador inglés cree que este formato junto a 'El Matador' sería todo un éxito, y el jefe de la UFC no lo ve con malos ojos
articles.summary: El peleador inglés cree que este formato junto a 'El Matador' sería todo un éxito, y el jefe de la UFC no lo ve con malos ojos
articles.body: Paddy Pimblett ha vuelto a hacer de las suyas y ha retado a Ilia Topuria a realizar juntos una nueva temporada de 'The Ultimate Fighter' para acabar peleando el año que viene, ya que considera que sería todo un éxito en un formato histórico dentro de la UFC. Además, tras el UFC 332 del pasado sábado Dana White -jefe de la UFC- fue preguntado al respecto, reconociendo que sería una gran idea para promocionar uno de los combates más esperados de los últimos tiempos en la promotora. 'The Ultimate Fighter' es un formato en el que dos equipos se baten en duelo en diferentes categorías de peso. Pimblett tendría su propio equipo y Topuria el suyo, y durante seis semanas se emitirían capítulos en los que los peleadores de ambos equipos se verían las caras en el octágono. Además, en dichos episodios también se mostraría el trabajo de Paddy e Ilia como entrenadores, así como la convivencia de ambos bandos. Otros peleadores históricos como Daniel Cormier, Conor McGregor o Alexander Volkanovski han pasado por este formato, y ahora ha sido Pimblett el que le ha propuesto a Topuria hacer lo mismo. "Creo que Topuria y yo daríamos pie a una temporada genial de 'The Ultimate Fighter'. Le sacaría tanto de quicio que cuando llegue el combate le finalizaría tan rápido como McGregor a Aldo", afirmó 'The Baddy' en una entrevista con Kolos MMA. De momento, Topuria no se ha pronunciado al respecto, ya que ni siquiera sabe quién será su próximo rival. 'El Matador' quiere una revancha contra Justin Gaethje, pero todo hace indicar que el peleador estadounidense se enfrentará a Arman Tsarukyan o se retirará. Por tanto, la pelea de Pimblett cobra cada vez más sentido, e incluso el propio Dana White cree que un 'The Ultimate Fighter' entre ambos es buen plan. "Me encanta la idea, pero muchas cosas determinan cómo se desarrollan estos enfrentamientos. Ciertas peleas o combates por el título dependen de otros factores, así que veremos como se desarrolla todo en el tiempo, pero sería una buena idea", reconoció el mandamás de la UFC tras el UFC 332. Eso sí, este tipo de propuestas tardan tiempo en realizarse, y ahora mismo la compañía está centrada en acabar 2026 por todo lo alto. Lo que está claro es que los caminos de Topuria y Pimblett están destinados a encontrarse. En una pelea titular, en un main event, en 'The Ultimate Fighter'... donde sea, pero esa rivalidad tiene todas las papeletas de terminarse pronto en un octágono de la UFC. Ambos son las dos mayores superestrellas a nivel mediático de peso ligero, por lo que su emparejamiento es inevitable.

articles.title: Sean O’Malley Reveals Private Voice Notes With Petr Yan, Admits He Will  “Duck” Payton Talbott if Yan Wins at UFC 333
articles.summary: Sean O'Malley reveals his banter with reigning champion Petr Yan over a potential title fight while addressing accusations from Payton Talbott.
articles.body:
The bantamweight title will be on the line at UFC 333 when Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili meet for their highly anticipated trilogy on October 24. Dvalishvili beat Yan in their first outing in 2023, but the Russian got his revenge at UFC 323 last December, snapping the Georgian's 14-fight winning streak.

One fighter who will be watching the co-main event closely is Sean O'Malley . "Suga" is riding a two-fight winning streak after beating Song Yadong at UFC 324 and knocking out Aiemann Zahabi at UFC Freedom 250.

O'Malley also has history with both Yan and Dvalishvili. Now, he has shared private messages with the reigning champion and hinted at his plans to reclaim the bantamweight title.

Sean O'Malley Responds to Payton Talbott's Ducking Accusations After His Latest Win

In a recent appearance on MMA Guru , the former bantamweight champion pulled up his Instagram exchange with Yan. The two traded playful warnings, with both seemingly open to a rematch if Yan gets past Dvalishvili at UFC 333.

O'Malley said, "I had some words to say with Petr over Instagram, and I would love to share it with you. These are, so I send him a voice message, and when he talks, he says, 'Sean, come to Abu Dhabi.' It's kinda hard to say, but this is what I say to him."

"Suga" then played his voice note for fans. He said, "Petr, what's up, buddy? Hope you're doing well. Hope you beat Merab so I can beat your ass again."

Yan was quick to fire back, replying, "Sure, hello. Coming to Abu Dhabi. I smash Merab up, and you will be next."

The exchange ended with both fighters laughing, and O'Malley couldn't resist taking a playful jab at his potential opponent. "Did you hear that laugh? One more time. Oh, little Petr. I like little Petr."

For context, O'Malley and Yan first met at UFC 280 in October 2022 in Abu Dhabi. The Arizona native walked away with a controversial split-decision victory, although many fans believed Yan had done enough to win.

That result ultimately helped O'Malley secure a title shot against Aljamain Sterling at UFC 292. He made the most of the opportunity, finishing Sterling in under two rounds to become the new 135-pound champion.

Now, O'Malley could be eyeing another shot at gold. However, he has also faced questions about allegedly avoiding rising contender Payton Talbott following the latter's knockout victory over Deiveson Figueredo at UFC 332.

O'Malley recently pushed back against those accusations , insisting that the UFC never offered him a fight against Talbott at UFC Freedom 250. He also made it clear that he would be willing to face the rising star.

He said, "I swear on my family, I did not get offered Payton Talbott at the White House… He called me out, and that sounds good." O'Malley then explained how the outcome of Yan's upcoming title fight could shape his next move.

O'Malley admitted, "Petr goes out there and loses, let's squabble. Me and Payton, let's make it happen. Petr goes out there and wins, I'm ducking him. I'm ducking him for a tougher fight… I'm ducking him for a Petr Yan. I fought four of the greatest bantamweights of all time in my last 7."

He continued, "Petr, Aljo, Merab and I beat Merab once, so I beat all three of the greatest bantamweights of all time. I ain't ducking!"

A Yan victory at UFC 333 could set up a rematch with O'Malley, giving the former champion a chance to settle their rivalry and reclaim the title. Meanwhile, another Dvalishvili win could leave O'Malley with a different decision to make, especially after losing to the Georgian twice.

With the title picture hanging in the balance, all eyes will be on UFC 333 to see who emerges as champion and whether O'Malley gets the rematch he wants or finally settles things with Talbott.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois expects to set up blockbuster fight Tyson Fury after Fabio Wardley rematch: 'That's what boxing's about'
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois, the WBO heavyweight world champion, expects to set up a blockbuster bout with Tyson Fury if they both win their next fights; Fury will meet Anthony Joshua in a December mega-fight while later this month Dubois rematches Fabio Wardley after an epic battle in their first bout
articles.body:
Dubois, the WBO world champion, thinks if he and Fury win their next fights they can then meet in another all-British heavyweight blockbuster.

Fury of course has a December 11 showdown with long-time rival Anthony Joshua, while Dubois will rematch Fabio Wardley on October 17.

Dubois has previously knocked out Joshua and believes Fury is an obvious future opponent.

"What a fight that would be. It's like me and AJ all over again. That sort of magnitude. That's what boxing's about really. Frank [Warren, their promoter] would love it, he's got both of us. I've got to come through my next fight and anything's possible," Dubois told Sky Sports News .

"I think Fury," Dubois said when asked who he thinks will win December's blockbuster showdown. "Everyone's been talking about this fight for such a long time. It'll be good to see them both get into the ring. Two legends of British boxing."

But he added: "Let's be real, I don't even care about that fight.

"I'm not looking past Fabio at all. One fight at a time. I'm just dedicating myself 100 percent to this fight and he's a true competitor, a true warrior and I'm just looking forward to getting in there and giving the fans another great fight."

Dubois won an extraordinary battle with Wardley in their first fight, picking himself up from the canvas twice early on to ultimately force the stoppage.

The Londoner thinks Wardley should have been pulled out of that fight sooner.

"They were gambling with him. Obviously he's known for getting bashed up and coming back so that's what they must have been gambling on. But I'm a different animal and I just keep getting stronger as the rounds go on," Dubois said.

"We're just going to do even better than the first time," he warned. "You'll see on the night."

He wants to finish Wardley earlier in the rematch: "A bit quicker, a bit more clinical.

"I can't wait to get back in there again and stick it on him again."

articles.title: Brandon Figueroa Breaks Hearts and Wins Belts
articles.summary: Brandon Figueroa makes the first defense of his featherweight world title on Oct. 17 in Las Vegas against former champion Tomoki Kameda.
articles.body:
WBA World Featherweight champion Brandon "The Heartbreaker" Figueroa will defend his title against former champion Tomoki Kameda of Japan in the co-main event on Saturday, October 17 at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas.

The Premier Boxing Champions card headlined by Sebastian Fundora against Ermal Hadribeaj is part of "The Fight" series airing live on TNT Sports and DAZN Boxing.

The Welasco, Texas native makes his first title defense after knocking out former champion Nick Ball in England in Februry.

Brandon Figueroa lived up to his moniker "The Heartbreaker" when he took the WBA World Featherweight title from Nick Ball in front of his hometown fans in Liverpool, England in February with a knockout win.

Now Figueroa of Welasco, Texas (27-2-1, 20 KOs) plans to deliver a successful first title defense against former champion Tomoki Kameda of Osaka, Japan (42-5, 23 KOs) on Saturday, October 17 at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas and presented by Premier Boxing Champions.

The co-main event puts Figueroa in front of a wider audience, airing as part of the new series "The Fight" on TNT Sports, the only regular series airing on linear television. It also airs on DAZN Boxing. It also puts the fight much closer to his Texas fans in Las Vegas than in Liverpool.

But Figueroa took the gamble by going to the champion's country, and the bet paid off in a spectacular performance with two knockdowns in the 12th round giving Figueroa the win.

It was the first loss of Ball's career, and the first two knockdowns of his career and knockout loss. At the time, Figueroa led on one card but trailed 106-103 on the other two. Without both knockdowns, Figueroa would have at best earned a draw. A single knockdown would have been a majority decision for Ball.

"If you saw me go up against all odds in Liverpool, you can imagine what I'm gonna do to defend my belt in Las Vegas," said Figueroa. "I'm coming with everything on October 17. I'm here to stay. I want to unify and fight the best. There's no style like mine. Tune in, you will be entertained."

Brandon Figueroa: "I'm Going To Make It Tough"

Already a two-division world champion, Figueroa fully embraced his underdog status, allowing it to motivate him to prove everyone wrong.

"For the Ball fight I was really motivated by the fact that he hadn't fought anyone like me," said Figueroa. "I showcased that in February. I already knew those fans were gonna be in for a surprise. I'm no pushover, and I'm not someone that you're gonna look good against. I'm gonna make it a tough fight, and I'm gonna be in your face the whole night."

Figueroa had the support of renowned trainer Manny Robles of Los Angeles. It was just their second fight working together. Figueroa credits Robles with bringing out a new side of his skill set that led to one of the best victories of his career.

"Manny just made sure I was being smart," said Figueroa. "Previously I was just going out there and showcasing my will. With Manny, he would tell me that he knows I have heart, but it's time to use your intelligence. He always says that I can box. He made me believe in my boxing skills more. I've benefited a lot from him. We have great chemistry together and with his whole team. We're a unit, and we're gonna keep showcasing that.

"Manny's guidance, intelligence, and experience have been vital to me. He's an old-school coach, and I just keep learning from him every day. He's very strategic and he trains me accordingly. I'm just like a sponge, learning anything I can from him."

On October 17, Figueroa will be facing an opponent he's crossed paths with before. Figueroa made his pro debut on the card featuring Kameda in the first of two memorable battles against Jamie McDonnell on May 9, 2015 in Texas.

Although Kameda recently lost a competitive decision to IBF World Featherweight champion Angelo Leo, Figueroa knows he'll have to combat Kameda's considerable experience to emerge victorious.

"Kameda is a veteran fighter, and a gritty fighter," said Figueroa. "He's got a lot of fights under his belt. He's got years of experience over me, so we don't take anything away from him. We've been watching his fights and breaking down what he does. I feel like they're gonna try to box me and emulate what Stephen Fulton Jr. did against me. He'll be prepared 100%, but I have to go out there and do my job and defend my belt."

Kameda, now 35, vows he will stick around until he wins a featherweight title and becomes a three-division world champion. He is nicknamed "El Mexicanito" for his offense-minded Mexican-style boxing.

Figueroa understands matchups against the featherweight division's fellow champions are within reach with a victory over Kameda. Figueroa believes that his own experience over the last decade give him a chance to emerge as the king of the featherweight division.

"Whoever is lined up for me, Manny and I will go to the drawing board and get ourselves ready," said Figueroa. "I obviously want the best of the best. If I have the opportunity to fight everyone and unify, it would be an honor.

I feel like I have the most experience out of all the champions, with Angelo Leo right under me. I think my resume and the fighters that I've fought speaks for itself."

Now age 35, Tomoki Kameda vows he will earn a featherweight world title before he retires. Photo: Lucas Noonan, Premier Boxing Champions

articles.title: Dana White Doubles Down on “Killer Instinct” Criticism of Ian Garry Over UFC 330 Fifth-Round Antics
articles.summary: Dana White has once again criticized Ian Garry for being overly friendly with Islam Makhachev during their welterweight title clash at UFC 330.
articles.body:
UFC 330 saw Islam Makhachev successfully defend his welterweight title for the first time, but the champion had to work for every second of the victory. Ian Garry pushed him through five grueling rounds, leaving Makhachev with a battered face and nose while giving him arguably his toughest test since his clash with Alexander Volkanovski at UFC 284.

Makhachev ultimately did enough to get his hand raised and extend his UFC winning streak to 17 fights. While Garry earned plenty of praise for making the champion work so hard, UFC CEO Dana White wasn't impressed with everything he saw from the Irishman.

White believes Garry's overly friendly approach may have cost him UFC gold . The 28-year-old showed plenty of respect for Makhachev throughout fight week, but he carried that same attitude into the Octagon. Between rounds, the two exchanged high-fives, fist bumps, and friendly pats. Garry even appeared to move in for a hug at the start of the fifth round, a moment that clearly rubbed White the wrong way.

The UFC boss has never been a fan of excessive camaraderie during a fight, and he previously criticized Garry's approach at the UFC 330 press conference. Nearly seven weeks after the Philadelphia showdown, White has now doubled down on his criticism, questioning whether the Irishman showed enough killer instinct when it mattered most.

Dana White Calls Out Ian Garry for Being Too Friendly With Islam Makhachev at UFC 330

During an appearance on Steven Bartlett's Diary of a CEO podcast, White read a placard that said, "You either have the killer instinct, or you don't."

White then said, "It says you either have the killer instinct, or you don't, and it's so true. So, this happened with Ian Garry. I felt like Ian Garry in that fifth round, you have this opportunity. You're fighting possibly the greatest fighter of all time. And you did a damn good f*cking job for four rounds. And, you know, he was battered. His whole right side was busted up, his face was busted up, but he was beating you as far as rounds go."

White felt Garry had everything to gain heading into the final five minutes, especially given his physical advantages and how competitive the fight had been. Instead, he believes the Irishman missed his chance to turn the tide.

He added, "Now, you're the younger, bigger, rangier fighter. You fought four incredible rounds. Get out there and put it on – you go out and start shaking his hands and hugging him. Do that when they're strapping the belt on you. Show Islam all the love you want when the fight's over."

White then explained why Garry's approach frustrated him so much, pointing out that the fifth round was his final opportunity to pull off a career-defining upset.

"This is the fifth round. You have five minutes to shock the world and, you know, everything you ever f*cking dreamed of and worked for can happen in these next five minutes. And you didn't do it."

When Bartlett pressed him on whether Garry lacked a clear killer instinct, White offered a more measured response but stood by his criticism.

He said, "I don't know. He's a classy, really nice guy. But that's not the time or place to be it. You have to go out, and you have five minutes left, you know. He didn't show it. If he does have it, he didn't show it."

Interestingly, Makhachev appeared to share some of White's confusion after UFC 330. During his post-fight press conference, the welterweight champion admitted that he didn't quite understand Garry's repeated displays of friendliness in the middle of such a competitive fight.

White's criticism raises an interesting question about where sportsmanship ends and competitive instinct takes over. When you're fighting for UFC gold against one of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world, even a small opening can make all the difference.

Now sitting at 17-2 following his loss to Makhachev, Garry will be looking for another opportunity to work his way back into the title picture. Michael Morales has also made his intentions clear in the 170lbs division, while Garry recently claimed that a potential matchup between them has been discussed and accused the undefeated contender of ducking him despite a date reportedly being locked in.

Whether that fight comes together remains to be seen. For now, Garry has another challenge ahead of him: proving that he can turn his competitive performances into a championship-winning result and, perhaps, change White's opinion of his killer instinct.

articles.title: Ki MMA: Scott Coker has 'unfinished business' amid launch of new promotion to 'shake up MMA'
articles.summary: Scott Coker says he has "something else to give" after some "unfinished business" following the launch of his new mixed martial arts promotion, Ki MMA.
articles.body:
Scott Coker says he has "something else to give" after some "unfinished business" following the launch of his new mixed martial arts promotion, Ki MMA.

Ki MMA, which is set to host its first event in 2027, is Coker's first business venture since he was president of Bellator, which was acquired by the PFL in 2023.

Since then the PFL has phased out the Bellator brand, before merging with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, but it's still unclear what its future looks like.

The UFC meanwhile, is in the first year of a seven-year broadcast deal with Paramount, and has faced criticism about fighter pay and matchmaking in the past 12 months.

Coker, 63, sees it as the perfect time to re-enter the MMA landscape.

"My body of work speaks for itself, I've done a lot in this sport and this space and I started coming to the conclusion that martial arts was in a bit of a funk," Coker told BBC Sport.

"The UFC had started their Paramount deal, PFL was shaking a bit, so I thought there needed to be something to shake up the sport again."

Ki MMA will feature a 32-fighter featherweight tournament, with events in North America, Europe, Asia and South America.

It also plans on featuring super fights from already established names within MMA, with Coker looking to sign free agents "in around two to three months".

The project is backed by $60m (£44.7m) in funding, with Coker promising that "fighters will come first and we'll treat them with respect".

Coker is regarded as a pioneer in MMA after being instrumental in the rise of former promotion Strikeforce.

Coker points to former UFC stars such as Daniel Cormier and Ronda Rousey as examples of fighters where he helped build their brand from scratch.

Cormier debuted in Strikeforce before winning UFC titles at light-heavyweight and heavyweight in a distinguished career.

Rousey, meanwhile, had fought two professional bouts prior to being signed by Coker, before going on to become one of the biggest MMA stars of all time.

Coker says his Ki MMA team have been searching gyms in cities such as Tokyo and Paris looking for "diamonds in the rough".

"I don't think anyone has built stars from scratch like we have in the past," said Coker.

"We will be in the star building business and the star searching business and that's what we're doing, searching for diamonds in the rough. We're gonna go mining.

"This is going to be a long distance race and take several years to build this group of fighters but the tournament speeds up the process."

Coker, who was born in South Korea, describes Ki as an East Asian word which means the "inner energy and spiritual journey of martial arts".

Coker has described Japan as the "birthplace of MMA" and wants his new promotion to reflect that.

A key change he wants to make is hosting Ki MMA fights in a ring as opposed to a cage, which was a key characteristic of former Japanese promotion Pride.

MMA fights are held in cages primarily to stop athletes falling out and to keep the action flowing, but Coker says it makes fights hard to see.

"I'm sitting right at the cage, and once they go to the side, I end up watching the whole fight on the big screen," Coker said.

"With the ring you have better viewing and more action because a fighter can't hold you against the cage and control you."

Coker says some details still need to be finalised but he's aiming to hold Ki MMA's first event early in 2027.

articles.title: Fury v Joshua: Murat Gassiev unsure if he is still WBA 'Super' champion
articles.summary: Murat Gassiev says he was "surprised" when he saw reports Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua would be for his WBA world title.
articles.body:
Murat Gassiev says he currently has no idea if he still is the WBA heavyweight champion after reports Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua would fight for his belt.

Gasiev, 32, was upgraded to 'Super' champion in July when Oleksandr Usyk vacated the title, having been the 'Regular' belt holder since 2025.

Fury and Joshua are scheduled to fight on 11 December in Cardiff and it was claimed that bout would be for the title Gassiev currently holds.

Speaking to ESPN , external and after reaching out to the WBA, Gassiev says he is still in the dark.

"[The] WBA give me big surprise about my belt. But in press conference when AJ and Fury have face off, I see only Ring Magazine belt, no WBA belt," Gassiev said.

"And to be honest right now, I don't have clear information about this situation. I don't know. Fight for 'Super' belt, another belt, I don't know.

"I check my email. I don't have any messages, any papers, but I'm not manager, promoter [or] lawyer. I'm fighter. I do my job, that's it."

The WBA recognise their 'Super' champion as their full champion, while the 'Regular' belt holder is often the number one contender to their world title.

There are four major world titles in boxing – the WBA 'Super', the IBF, the WBC and the WBO belts.

Gassiev is still listed on the WBA's website as their reigning champion, with Fury ranked number two behind American Jarrell Miller and Joshua at three.

Joshua and Fury are both two-time heavyweight world champions and held a launch news conference last week in London.

The heavyweights will meet at Cardiff's Principality stadium after a decade-long effort to bring the British rivals together in the ring.

WBO world champion Daniel Dubois, who has a knockout win over Joshua, says he cannot pick a winner.

"It doesn't seem like it has that same edge to it, if it happened years ago," Dubois said.

"They missed the fire and the edge. But I am sure it will be a great fight regardless."

articles.title: Paddy Pimblett insiste en hacer The Ultimate Fighter contra Ilia Topuria: "No sabría dónde mirar..."
articles.standfirst: El peleador inglés sigue empeñado en medirse a 'El Matador' en el reality más famoso de la UFC
articles.summary: El peleador inglés sigue empeñado en medirse a 'El Matador' en el reality más famoso de la UFC
articles.body: Paddy Pimblett tiene una misión: provocar a Lis Topuria para que acepte medirse a él en la nueva temporada de 'The Ultimate Fighter'. El peleador inglés lleva días empeñado en llamar la atención de 'El Matador' con una propuesta que el mismísimo Dana White ve con buenos ojos, aunque el peleador hispanogeorgiano sigue sin responder a estos cantos de sirena. Hace unos días, 'The Baddy' afirmó que si realiza este reality ante Topuria le sacaría de quicio y la finalizaría antes que Conor McGregor a José Aldo, ya que sabe que tiene que hacer todo lo posible para calentar esta pelea y que sea el siguiente paso que quiera tomar la compañía. Ilia, por su parte, preferiría una revancha contra Justin Gaethje, pero todo indica que no será posible. "Tendría su cabeza en el cobertizo durante seis semanas. No sabría dónde mirar, qué decir. Lo tendría sintiéndose incómodo constantemente. Ilia y yo traeríamos las audiencias de vuelta a 'The Ultimate Fighter'", afirmó Pimblett en su canal de Youtube. Lo cierto es que este reality fue durante una época un gran bastión para la UFC, con enfrentamientos históricos y superestrellas formando parte del mismo. Sin embargo, a día de hoy poca gente está interesada en seguirlo, por lo que el objetivo de Paddy es convencer a la UFC de que si lo hacen entre él y Topuria podrían revivir un formato que durante una época fue todo un éxito. Es cierto que tanto Ilia como el peleador inglés ya son dos superestrellas de la compañía, por lo que no tienen necesidad de darse a conocer más en un formato largo con el que no se enfrentarían hasta mediados de 2027, pero a su vez hay mucha gente esperando que el beef entre ambos se magnifique a través de la pantalla. Lo normal es que, en caso de que se vean las caras, sea en un combate estelar de un evento numerado, sin 'The Ultimate Fighter' de por medio, pero en este deporte tan impredecible nunca se sabe. Eso sí, si a Ilia de veras le interesase esta idea ya habría respondido, pero de momento se mantiene en silencio absoluto. Sus planes seguramente sean otros, por lo que se esperan noticias sobre su futuro antes de que se acabe el año.

articles.title: Denzel Bentley is fighting to keep his world title on the line for Shane Mosley Jr clash with ongoing WBO appeal
articles.summary: Denzel Bentley doesn't want to vacate his world title and is appealing to the WBO to sanction his fight with Shane Mosley Jr as a voluntary defence; Watch Bentley vs Mosley Jr on the Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke bill on November 7 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The WBO has instructed Bentley to make an immediate title defence against mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez, while Bentley is committed to boxing Shane Mosley Jr next on November 7 at the Copper Box Arena in London.

Bentley is convinced he should have the right to make a voluntary defence against Mosley and remain champion.

Mosley Jr, the son of boxing star Shane Mosley, is rated No 6 with the WBO and a legitimate title contender after a stunning stoppage win over Serhii Bohachuk in his last fight.

"I'm more than happy to fight Hernandez. It's just the situation at hand. We already thought we were fighting a voluntary defence before the end of the year and put things in place for that. This has been thrown on us," Bentley told Sky Sports .

"It just makes it a difficult place for me to be in. I don't want to vacate and I don't want to be stripped of my title. But I have to move forward in my career and I cannot wait around for people to make decisions for me."

His appeal with the WBO is ongoing. "I think because it went to purse bids it's making it a bit difficult at this point. I think we do have a good case. I did become champion and in their rulings you get nine months from when you become champion until your the mandatory gets called on. We've been fighting this case from before it went to purse bids," Bentley said.

"I think we've got a strong enough case for us to keep our title and if we can keep the title on the line for this fight, it would be an honour for me and an honour for Shane Mosley Jr getting a shot at a world title and he could potentially become world champion. Not on my watch, I'm not going to let that happen."

When it comes to his upcoming battle in the ring, Bentley is expecting an exciting clash with Mosley Jr on November 7, live on Sky Sports .

"He is on a good run right now," the Londoner said of Mosley. "He's a tough guy, he's got a lot of heart and it's going to be a tough fight.

"I think it's going to be a little bit of a dogfight. He is a dog, he's got heart, he's a workhorse, he's very fit, he throws a lot of punches.

"We're going to give a good fight for the fans."

Watch Bentley fight Mosley Jr on the Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke bill on November 7 live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: Sal Everett, el asistente de Dana White que se juega un contrato con la UFC esta madrugada
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense, que lleva años trabajando como empleado del mandamás de la promotora, se enfrentará a Ozzy Martín con el objetivo de ganarse el puesto
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense, que lleva años trabajando como empleado del mandamás de la promotora, se enfrentará a Ozzy Martín con el objetivo de ganarse el puesto
articles.body: Cuando parecía que se habia visto todo en el mundo de las MMA, Sal Everett (4-0) ha doblado la apuesta. Esta madrugada se celebrará el noveno episodio de la décima temporada de las Dana White's Contender Series, y en uno de los combates el peleador estadounidense se enfrentará a Ozzy Díaz (4-0) con el objetivo de ganarse un contrato en la UFC. Lo destacable no es la pelea en sí, sino que Everett lleva varios años trabajando como asistente de Dana White, lo que añade mucho más misticismo a la trama, ya que podría ser contratado por el que ya es su jefe en otra faceta dentro de la promotora. Everett lleva siendo miembro de la seguridad de la UFC desde hace tres años, y al poco tiempo comenzó su andadura en las MMA. Desde entonces ha compaginado ambos trabajos, y ha ascendido desde seguridad hasta convertirse en asistente de Dana White y de los directivos de la UFC. "Estaba en el equipo del turno de noche cuando me contrataron por primera vez. Solo estuve en el turno de noche hasta julio, porque recuerdo que mi primera semana como asistente de Dana fue la Semana Internacional de la Lucha. Una locura total. Una semana de locos. Ha sido una experiencia increíble. Recuerdo trabajar en el turno de noche, caminando por el APEX, caminando por el octágono, sin tener la visión al 100%. De hecho, no la tenía al 100%. Pero con cada pelea, la visión se fue aclarando", afirmó en una entrevista con MMA Junkie. Aunque Dana White no suele ser el que selecciona a los peleadores, seguramente haya metido mano para que Sal pueda buscarse un contrato en la promotora. Es cierto que en las DWCS no te vale solo con ganar, pero una finalización seguramente le baste para que el mandamás de la UFC reparta uno de los contratos más gratificantes desde que inició este formato. "Lo aprecio mucho. Es amigo mío, mi jefe. Es un día más en la oficina. Ha asistido a la mayoría de mis peleas. Para mí no es nada nuevo, y definitivamente siento que tengo que esforzarme más porque la gente está invirtiendo en mí, creyendo en mí. Yo creo en mí mismo, así que solo estoy devolviendo el cariño que recibo. Cada día que estoy en la UFC me motiva, ver a los campeones allí y a tipos como Merab siendo tan humildes. Esos tipos me motivaron. Poder trabajar en esos vestuarios y ser invitado a entrenar con ellos, ver que no hay diferencia con estos campeones... todo se reduce al trabajo que tengo que hacer", finalizó Everett. De momento, el peleador estadounidense ha finalizado los ocho combates que ha disputado en su carrera -cuatro en amateur y cuatro en profesional-, por lo que quiere hacer lo propio esta noche ante un rival que tampoco conoce la decisión de los jueces pero que sí ha sido finalizado en su carrera amateur.

articles.title: Diego Lopes reveals UFC discussed 2 other lightweight fights before Charles Oliveira
articles.summary: Lopes, who's fought primarily as a featherweight in the UFC, is set to make his 155-pound debut against Charles Oliveira for the BMF title at UFC 335.
articles.body:
Diego Lopes is still a hot commodity despite his recent UFC title fight losses.

During the UFC 332 broadcast this past Saturday, the promotion announced that Lopes is set to move up to the lightweight division to headline the year's final numbered UFC event — UFC 335 on Dec. 12 in Las Vegas — and challenge Charles Oliveira for the ceremonial BMF title. Speaking Tuesday on "The Ariel Helwani Show," Lopes, who has fought primarily as a featherweight in the UFC, explained why now was the time to move up in weight.

"Now I think I'm in the steadiest position for a move to 155 [pounds], because I lost two times to [Alexander Volkanovski]," Lopes told Uncrowned. "I won my last fight at 145. We don't have a lot of options at 145 now, and I wanted to make the move for fun fights at 155.

"It depends [whether I'll go back down]. I'm going to feel my body, my power, my strength, and conditioning at 155. After this fight, we're going to check if I can [stay or go back]. Now, my weight is still good. I can come down for 145 if the UFC needs in the future."

Lopes, 31, said he's talked with his team about moving up in weight classes for a long time. And while he's fought as low as bantamweight in the pre-UFC years of his career, Lopes has somehow awkwardly avoided coming into a fight right at 155 pounds, having had previous catchweight bouts at both 150 and 165 pounds.

Two months out from UFC 335, Lopes said he's around 175 pounds and believes he's a perfect stylistic fit for a BMF title fight. That, however, wasn't his only fight option.

"My first option when I talked to UFC was to take the main event with Dan Hooker in Paris, but UFC signed the French guy [Salahdine Parnasse], and I didn't take this fight," Lopes said. "They said Charles Oliveira. If it's not possible, maybe 'BSD' (Benoit Saint Denis) in New York. So UFC did the fight with Oliveira, and I'm happy with this fight."

It's been all gas and no brakes for Lopes since he arrived in the UFC in May 2023. Lopes' most recent win — a second-round knockout of Steve Garcia at UFC Freedom 250 at the White House — was his 10th fight in the promotion.

Coincidentally, Lopes' departure from 145 pounds comes ahead of the next title fight between the only two fighters he's lost to in the promotion: UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski and top-ranked contender Movsar Evloev, who meet on Oct. 24 at UFC 333.

Lopes believes he'll be in a great spot regardless of the winner of Volkanovski vs. Evloev, but he knows he has his hands full with Oliveira first.

"If 'Volk' wins, it's good for me. If Movsar wins, it's good for me too, because I lost to both guys. So I don't care," Lopes said. "But I hope 'Volk' can take this fight and can finish his career very well. He's a legend of the sport and maybe one of the top three, top five guys of all time.

"He's one of the best in the world and deserves to finish his career very well."

articles.title: AEW Grand Slam France Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From Dynamite in Paris
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of AEW Dynamite's Grand Slam France special on October 6.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of AEW Dynamite's Grand Slam France special on October 6.

Here's a look at what AEW advertised for the show:

Jon Moxley and Gabe Kidd vs. Jake Doyle and Mark Davis

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's special Tuesday episode of Dynamite.

Kofi got his first chance to win a singles title in AEW when he challenged Bandido for the ROH World Heavyweight Championship. This also continues the growing feud between Brodido and the trio of Swerve Strickland and New Level.

They started off with some simple exchanges and taunts to get the crowd to react, but they didn't rush right into the fast-paced or high-flying stuff. It took a couple of minutes before they started picking up the pace.

Swerve and Prince Nana eventually showed up to lend Kofi some support, and Adam Page and Brody King were not far behind to back up Bandido.

Bandido and Kofi barely have any experience working together, but they developed chemistry right away and put on a fun show for the Paris crowd. They definitely paced themselves in places, but it didn't slow down the match enough to affect it too much.

Things eventually broke down at ringside as Hangman and Swerve got into it, but their respective allies pulled them apart. Bandido took advantage of the distraction and hit the 21 Plex for the pin and the win.

It's so cool getting to watch Kofi and Austin Creed get to face a whole new roster after they both spent so long in WWE.

Kofi's dive over the top rope early in the match looked good.

Excalibur made an effort to say Adidas the way they say it in Europe, which was kind of funny.

Jack Perry has been trying to get Samoa Joe's attention in recent weeks, and he finally got his match this week against the former world champion.

Jungle Jack ran right at Joe as soon as the bell rang, but the big man was ready for him. Perry hit a couple of chops in the corner, and Joe almost looked insulted that he thought it would do anything, so he shoved him to the mat.

Perry remained aggressive and finally scored a takedown with a huge clothesline that caught Joe off guard. The Samoan Submission Machine hit one big slam to turn things around.

While Perry continued to show life and fight back, Joe definitely controlled the pace for most of the match. That being said, Jack got in a lot more offense than a lot of people probably expected.

Joe sold well for him and made him look like a tough fighter. This match made good use of the time they were given, and it may have even lasted a bit longer than necessary, but that did not feel like a negative.

After a solid back-and-forth fight, Joe hit the Muscle Buster for the win.

Joe looked genuinely surprised when Perry hit the clothesline.

Joe's walkaway spot is still undefeated.

Perry tried to hit a piledriver. As you would probably expect, he was not successful in picking Joe up.

Joe could be heard audibly swearing at one point.

Moxley and Kidd teamed up this week to battle Don Callis Family members, Jake Doyle and Mark Davis, in tag team action.

Kidd started the match by delivering a series of chops to Davis, but it barely seemed to rattle him. Doyle tagged in for a double-team spot, so Mox tagged in to take on Doyle.

The weird thing about this match is that neither team had any outright babyfaces. Davis, Doyle and Kidd are objectively heels, and Mox treads closer to the tweener line. That didn't stop the crowd from choosing to cheer for the Death Riders and boo the DCF, though.

This was a high-energy match that was all over the place, but in a good way. All four men brought a lot of intensity and hard-hitting action to the ring. Every one of them is going to need at least an ice pack after this one.

This match stole the first hour of the show, which is saying a lot when you look at who else competed before them. Davis ended up scoring the win for his team by pinning Kidd, which many would consider an upset. Mox looked very mad after the bell.

Result: Davis and Doyle defeat Moxley and Kidd

The Death Riders still have a chair for Pac during their entrance.

Moxley is deceptively big these days. You don't really realize it until you see him next to another big guy and he is close to the same size.

Davis is well regarded in AEW, and he is still vastly underrated. His national title run was not long enough.

Kidd might be the only person who can make Moxley looks like a calm and measured person.

Darby Allin vs. Kyle Fletcher (TNT Championship)

After a little bit of trash talk, Allin and Fletcher started throwing punches right away to kick their TNT title match off with some energy.

At just a couple of minutes into the match, Allin jumped off the top rope to put Fletcher through the timekeeper's table, so they were not holding back or taking it slow. They were trying to make sure they stole the show.

It felt like every match on this card was better than the last, and more physical, too. Allin and Fletcher delivered what some would call a PPV-quality match, but that seems to be a weekly occurrence in AEW anyway.

Fletcher, the former TNT champion used his size and power to bully his much smaller opponent when he got the chance, and Allin was his usual risk-taking self. They meshed their styles together perfectly to deliver an entertaining performance.

Allin was busted wide open and dripping blood all over the mat toward the end, but he still had some fight in him. He was able to put Fletcher away to retain his title, but it was a struggle.

The suicide dive Allin hit might be one of the best ones he has ever done. Fletcher sold it perfectly, too.

Fletcher might not have been selling when he was walking a little slower. He took some big bumps.

Something about the way Fletcher hits a simple bodyslam makes it look so much more brutal than most. He really gets people high up and then slams them with velocity.

Mercedes Mone vs. Queen Aminata (Women's World Championship)

Aminata had her biggest AEW match to date this week when she challenged Mercedes for the women's world title.

Aminata has been on the rise in AEW recently. She is scoring more wins and keeps finding herself with big opportunities, but management has yet to fully flip the switch on her push and put a title around her waist.

Mone was giving up a little size to her opponent, but not enough for it to make her an underdog, so she played the part of a bully champion well, which helped Aminata get the crowd behind her without much effort.

There was a lot to like in this match. Both women were throwing their bodies into everything they did. This was definitely Aminata's best performance to date, and yet another on the long list of fun matches Mercedes has had in AEW.

After The CEO got the win, Thekla immediately came out and attacked her with a Spear. The Toxic Spider went for a stomp, but Mercedes escaped before she could do it.

Aminata gave an interview before the match and spoke fluent French, which makes since because she used to live there.

Mercedes always kills it with the gear, but Aminata had some cool gear, too.

The CEO got some cheap heat by stomping on a beret, which is the funniest possible way to insult the country of France.

It felt like the commercial came earlier in the match than usual.

articles.title: “Not have been able to go without his help”: How Conor McGregor turned from a hero into a helping hand for two 13-year-old fans with a €10,000 heartwarming move
articles.summary: For Adam and Dylan Duffy, Conor McGregor had always been the fighter they looked up to.
articles.body: For Adam and Dylan Duffy, Conor McGregor had always been the fighter they looked up to. The Ballycanew twins had started their own MMA journey and dreamed of competing on a bigger stage. Then, in June 2022, McGregor noticed their fundraiser and stepped in with €10,000. The donation did more than help two young fighters reach Abu Dhabi. It gave them a moment they never expected from the man they had followed for years.Conor McGregor gave the twins €10,000 when they needed it mostAdam and Dylan had earned places on the Irish MMA Youth International Team and were preparing for the IMMAF Youth World Championships in Abu Dhabi in 2022. But getting there came with a cost. The twins launched a fundraiser with a target of around €6,000 to cover their trip.Their mother, Liz Duffy, also tried to spread the word online. She tagged McGregor in social media posts and hoped he might share the boys' story. Instead, the former UFC champion did something much bigger.In June 2022, McGregor donated €10,000 to the fundraiser. He then commented online: “Done! Do the land proud I know.” The donation pushed the twins beyond their original target and gave them the financial support they needed for the trip.The reaction from Adam showed just how much the moment meant to them. Speaking to the Gorey Guardian in June 2022 after learning about the donation, Adam said he was at training when his coach told him about it.Surprisingly, Adam initially thought his coach was joking until he saw McGregor’s comment himself. He even joked that he now felt he had to win because McGregor had donated the money.“I was going insane!I thought he was joking until he showed me the comments. I feel like I have to win now because he donated all that money.’ Adam said.Dylan also understood how important the donation could be. Speaking to the Gorey Guardian in June 2022, he said the brothers might not have been able to make the trip without McGregor’s help.He said, “We might not have been able to go without his help. There are so many gyms out there and he donated to us, which is insane.”That made the gesture more personal. The twins had spent years watching McGregor compete. Now, the UFC star had helped them take the next step in their own MMA careers. The €10,000 gift became bigger than one tripThe twins did not stop fundraising after McGregor's donation. Adam and Dylan, along with their parents Jason and Liz, planned to use extra funds to buy equipment for their coach Richie Ivory’s gym and help other Irish fighters travel to the IMMAF World Championships. They also planned to support the Waterford Neonatal Unit, where the twins were born.The brothers had already spent four years training with Ivory before the 2022 championship opportunity. They first joined his jiu-jitsu classes after he returned to Ireland from Australia. Their training later moved toward MMA, where both boys developed a strong interest in the sport.McGregor’s €10,000 donation therefore did not simply cover a plane ticket. It helped two young Irish fighters chase a dream they had worked toward for years.For Adam and Dylan, there was also a personal reward. After receiving the donation, they hoped to meet McGregor at his pub and thank him themselves. Adam even joked, “I’m basically friends with Conor now!"For two 13-year-old fighters who had grown up admiring McGregor, getting help from their hero was already an unforgettable chapter. articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Murat Gassiev says WBA world title decision is 'strange' and he should be mandatory for Fury-AJ winner
articles.summary: Murat Gassiev has criticised the WBA for not elevating him to full world championship status and says it's "strange" to sanction Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua as a fight for the 'super' title; Gassiev believes he should now be made the mandatory challenger for the Fury vs Joshua winner
articles.body:
Gassiev, the WBA 'regular' titlist, believed he would be upgraded to 'super' or full world champion when Oleksandr Usyk vacated the belt.

It has subsequently emerged that the WBA intend to make the Fury vs Joshua fight on December 11 for the 'super' title, essentially making Gassiev a secondary belt-holder.

That decision baffled the Russian. "This situation is interesting, a little bit strange, with the belt," Gassiev told Sky Sports .

"When Usyk left his belt, I wake up I'm super champion. Go to sleep, wake up, I'm again regular champion. It's okay. I'm not angry. I understand. I'm not a kid, I understand everything."

But he does believe the WBA must then install him as the mandatory challenger for the winner.

"From me a big present for AJ and Tyson before new year. A present from me. Just only one thing. Who wins - after the fight I need to fight with this guy for sure," he declared.

"I think it's a good option and I'm happy for this if this situation happens. I'm happy and I'm ready."

He thinks that winner will be Fury. "Fury is my favourite fighter," Gassiev said. "I like his style. How he does everything. I think Tyson wins by decision, or AJ by knockout."

He added: "I love him outside the ring, but inside the ring I don't love anybody. It's sport. It's nothing personal. This is only sport for me. When the fight finishes I shake hands, hug and I can be friends with this guy."

Gassiev last boxed in June when he stopped Peter Kadiru and has no date confirmed for his next fight.

"I'm only training right now. I have people who speak with WBA and right now all my focus is only for training," he said.

"I'm a fighter. I'm not manager, I'm not promoter. I just want to fight and do my job. I'm just waiting for what happens next."

articles.title: Boxing: Derek Chisora, 42, says he will fight in December after deciding against retirement
articles.summary: Derek Chisora's last fight was billed as his retirement bout, but the 42-year-old says he intends to box in December.
articles.body:
Derek Chisora says he is not retiring and will fight again in December.

The 42-year-old Briton lost to Deontay Wilder in April in what was billed as his 50th and final fight.

However, Chisora has since refused to confirm his retirement. Speaking at a news conference on Tuesday, said he believed he would fight in December against Murat Gassiev.

"December will be me versus Gassiev," Chisora said.

"We're going to decide where, either in London or Manchester. We're going to put two belts on the line, I believe, the IBA and the one Gassiev holds.

"What people have to understand is that what the IBA does is unbelievable. I believe this goes deeper than that we're doing here right now.

"I believe it's going to get better and better. In December we'll be fighting."

Gassiev is currently the WBA 'super' heavyweight world champion, but his status is unclear after reports claimed Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua would be fighting for his world title in their contest on 11 December.

The Russian said on Tuesday he was unsure if he remained the WBA's world champion.

Chisora's news conference was hosted by the IBA, the body that was stripped of its status as amateur boxing's governing body by the International Olympic Committee in 2023 and has since been staging professional bouts.

Gassiev's recent bouts have been under the IBA's banner and he was upgraded to the WBA's 'super' champion in June after Oleksandr Usyk relinquished the belt.

Several of Chisora's recent bouts have been billed as farewell fights and there have been repeated calls from people within the boxing community for the veteran to retire because of his age.

Chisora has 36 wins in 50 fights and defended his decision to continue fighting.

"I never said I was retired. They (the organisers) said '50 last dance'," he said.

"This is why you've got [films like] Rush Hour 1, Rush Hour 2, Coming to America 1, coming to America 2. You understand?

"So this is the Last Dance 3. Listen, trust me, I'm a seller, I sell. That's my job."
