articles.title: UFC: Former employee Sal Everett wins fighter contract with first-round knockout
articles.summary: Former UFC employee Sal Everett wins a fighter contract with the promotion after knocking out Ozzy Martin in Dana White's Contender Series.
articles.body:
Just a few months ago, Sal Everett was working for the UFC as a security guard and runner - now he's earned a contract to fight for the promotion.

In Dana White's Contender Series, the 29-year-old knocked out fellow American Ozzy Martin with a devastating combination in the first round.

UFC president White awarded Everett a contract with the promotion after the victory, before admitting he struggled to contain his excitement after watching him win.

"That's why I got up and walked out after he won, I don't want to be overly celebrating," said White.

"Sal is one of the greatest kids ever and it couldn't happen to a better person - I'm happy for him.

"I think this contract changes his life so he doesn't have to work at the office."

Everett joined the UFC about three years ago as a security guard, before later becoming a runner for White, doing errands.

Everett trained in MMA while working for the UFC and won the first four fights of his career before being offered a spot in the Contender Series.

He recently left his job at the UFC so he could focus on his career as a professional fighter.

"Hey boss, I'm ready to be in the UFC," Everett said during his post-fight interview.

"The whole division, you know my name. I'm not backing down from any challenges."

Everett's win comes one week after Briton George Staines' victory , where he won a UFC contract after stopping Loai Abushaar inside 61 seconds.

articles.body: Several Indian wrestlers, including 2024 U17 World Champion Neha Sangwan, have been refused US visas, putting their participation in the U23 World Wrestling Championships in Las Vegas from October 12 to 18 in doubt.The wrestlers were verbally told that their visa applications had been refused because they were below 20 years of age and unemployed. En total, y hasta la fecha, tres triunfos y una derrota para el peleador español de origen marroquí. Tras dicho combate, sobre todo si se resuelve con victoria, se abrirá un periodo de 'elección' para el de Torre Pacheco. articles.body: Matheus “Jaguar” Camilo is a Brazilian mixed martial artist competing in the UFC lightweight division. The 25-year-old has built momentum in the promotion after winning two straight fights. Camilo enters his next bout against Jai Herbert with an 11-3-0 professional record and a 2-1 UFC record.Known for his explosive style and pressure fighting, the Brazilian will look to continue his rise when he faces the experienced British veteran at UFC Fight Night: Allen vs Duncan on October 10.Who is Matheus Camilo?Born on January 2, 2001, in Rio Branco, Acre, Brazil, Matheus Camilo began his journey in Brazilian MMA before moving to Rio de Janeiro. He later continued his development on the U.S. regional circuit and eventually earned his opportunity to compete in the UFC.Camilo fights under the nickname “Jaguar.” He stands 5 feet 10 inches tall and competes at 155 pounds in the lightweight division. He uses an orthodox stance and trains out of Xtreme Couture in Las Vegas, while also having links to the Nova Uniao team.Camilo currently holds a professional record of 11 wins and three losses. His UFC record stands at 2-1. His recent run has helped him establish himself as an interesting young lightweight prospect.The Brazilian earned his UFC contract after defeating Dorobshokh Nabotov. He won at Z Fight Night 2 in late 2024. However, his promotional debut did not go according to plan.Camilo suffered a loss to Gabe Green in May 2025. It was his first UFC appearance. However, he soon responded to the setback.In November 2025, Camilo returned to the Octagon. He secured a unanimous decision victory over Viacheslav Borshchev.He then delivered an even more impressive performance. Especially in his bout against Nazim Sadykhov at UFC Baku in June 2026. articles.title: Damar Thomas, GB super-heavy and new European silver medallist: 'I want to add my name to that list of Olympic greats'
articles.summary: Rising super-heavyweight Damar Thomas won the silver medal at the recent European championships; Commonwealth Games gold medallist Thomas is resisting the temptations of professional boxing to focus on the LA Olympic Games in 2028: "Nothing will stop me from doing that"
articles.body:
Thomas is a gifted amateur boxer, he won the Commonwealth Games this year and most recently reached the final of the European championships.

Already, clearly, he would be a tremendous prospect in professional boxing. For a heavyweight of such potential, there will be lucrative opportunities to turn pro early on in an Olympic cycle.

It may be tempting but Thomas is keeping his focus on LA 2028.

"I'd be lying if I said it wasn't, but it's all noise at the end of the day and I've always wanted to go to the Olympics, ever since I got into boxing and saw all the Olympic greats I wanted to add my name to that list," Thomas said.

He added: "I think it'll be great. Paris was a good Olympics but I think LA will be even better."

Since a loss to near-legendary Cuban Julio La Cruz at last year's World championships, Thomas has been on a fantastic winning run. His only defeat in the last 12 months came in the European championship final when he boxed Russia's David Surov for the first time.

"Everyone hates losing but it's all a part of the journey," Thomas said.

"You want to face everyone before the Olympics because that's when it really matters. All these tournaments are learning so when it comes to the LA Olympics you've boxed everyone, you know how they are.

"I look forward to sharing the ring with him again hopefully, which I'm sure we will."

Winning a European silver medal is still a major achievement, rare for a GB boxer.

"It's a great feeling and it's all a part of the process," Thomas said. "We train to prepare for all styles. Nothing we haven't seen before. Especially when you're in the European final, you expect nothing less, you're both the best operators in Europe.

"I've been in the ring with him now so I know what to expect… Everyone's human at the end of the day and everyone's beatable.

"It's the long nights and the early mornings all paying off," he added. "It's all the hard work I've put into it and I'm definitely getting something out of it."

The experiences he's getting now, boxing the best in the amateur sport at senior level, entering the biggest tournaments and winning medals, will stand him in good stead for when he eventually turns professional.

"The Olympics are only two years away so all these tournaments matter," Thomas said. "It goes in the blink of an eye, especially when you're out boxing every other month and going to these training camps, it goes in the blink of an eye.

"So we try to get as many bouts as we can under us. We've faced everyone, we've been in with every style, so it won't come as a shock to us."

Modern British boxing has a vibrant heavyweight scene, spearheaded by Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury.

Thomas is looking forward to leading the next generation of British heavyweights.

"It'll be great, especially once I've won this Olympic gold, it'll be great to add my name to the list and carry it on," he said.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Cardiff Council asked to approve 1am ringwalk at Principality Stadium
articles.summary: An application has been made to Cardiff Council for the ringwalk for the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight to take place at 1am; They would like the premises also open until 3.30am; It has been described as a 'very limited, one-off occasion'
articles.body:
The Principality Stadium will host the biggest fight in British boxing history, with the bout being billed as taking place on Friday December 11.

However, the expected schedule for the showdown has now been revealed, which will see the main event take place in the early hours of Saturday morning UK time.

An application to Cardiff Council confirmed the ringwalk is planned to start at around 1am, after a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 3.30am.

Those timings would suit peak viewing time in the United States, with Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh, his American business partner Dana White and broadcasters Netflix having originally pushed for New York's Madison Square Garden as the venue.

Despite Cardiff being announced as the venue last month, required changes to its premises licence to allow the early-hours fight to go ahead have yet to be secured.

In a bid to obtain the necessary permissions, Millennium Stadium plc has applied to the council to extend timings at the venue "on a very limited one-off occasion".

The application seeks to extend permitted hours for boxing and wrestling entertainment from an existing cut-off of 1am to 3am on December 12.

A council spokesperson said: "This is to facilitate the proposed Anthony Joshua v Tyson Fury bout, with the ringwalk commencing at 1am."

The licence variation seeks an extension for live music on the same date, to facilitate a short live performance immediately before the ring walk.

It also proposes an extension for recorded music, late-night refreshment and supply of alcohol until 3am, with the stadium closing time being moved to 3.30am.

The applicants added that the roof will be shut throughout the event and enhanced security and stewarding arrangements will be in place.

An application to vary a premises licence must be advertised, including by displaying a notice at or on the premises, for 28 consecutive days.

Members of the public and other authorities may make an objection to the Principality Stadium application, or a comment in support, until November 3.

If no relevant representations are received, the council must grant the application.

If objections are made, then a council hearing will be held to consider them.

This may result in modifications to the conditions of the licence, or the application may be refused altogether.

After the fight was announced last month, Cardiff Council leader Chris Weaver said: "The contest at Principality Stadium has the potential to bring significant economic benefits to the city and attract visitors from across the UK and beyond.

"Major events provide a welcome boost for local businesses, support jobs and showcase Cardiff to a global audience.

"There are still some arrangements to be finalised with the organisers, including any required changes to Principality Stadium's premises licence, but we are looking forward to welcoming fans to the city for what promises to be an unforgettable night of boxing."

articles.title: Así es Abdul Hussein, el próximo rival de Hecher Sosa en la UFC
articles.standfirst: El peleador finlandés se medirá al español el próximo 28 de noviembre en el UFC Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: El peleador finlandés se medirá al español el próximo 28 de noviembre en el UFC Abu Dhabi
articles.body: Esta misma mañana se ha hecho oficial el combate entre Hecher Sosa (15-1) y Abdul Hussein (16-2) de cara al próximo 28 de noviembre en el UFC Abu Dhabi. Este enfrentamiento significará el segundo combate en la compañía del peleador español, que ya debutó a lo grande el pasado marzo ante Luan Lacerda. En esta ocasión se medirá a otro gran prospecto del peso gallo como el finlandés, que al igual que el canario solo tiene una pelea en la promotora y también ganó, en su caso por sumisión. Hussein nació en Beirut -Líbano- y proviene de una familia de refugiados palestinos que se vieron obligados a emigrar a Finlandia cuando Hussein era pequeño. El peleador finlandés, criado en campos de refugiados, encontró su amor por las MMA en 2014 y en 2016 ya era profesional. Su amor por el deporte surgió de idolatrar a Demetrious Johnson y de ver 'The Ultimate Fighter', aunque pasaría una década hasta que dio el salto a la UFC en 2026. Con 18 años, Hussein se coronó como campeón de Europa IMMAF, y un año después fue campeón mundial para agrandar aún más su palmarés a una corta edad. Sus 15 victorias antes de llegar a la UFC fueron por finalización, con cinco K.O. y nueve sumisiones, y de sus dos derrotas solo fue sometido en una de ellas. Abdul tiene buen poder de K.O., aunque destaca por sus habilidades en el grappling y en la pelea en suelo, tal y como demostró en su debut en la UFC, donde superó a un duro veterano como Cody Gibson por sumisión en el tercer asalto después de un gran combate. Por tanto, la clave para la victoria de Hecher pasará por el striking, donde a priori es superior al finlandés. Es un rival difícil, incómodo y completo, pero el 'Guanche Warrior' ya ha demostrado en más de una ocasión que es capaz de desenvolverse en cualquier tipo de circunstancias. En su debut ya se enfrentó a un experto en jiu-jitsu como Lacerda y salió airoso, por lo que está vez hará todo lo posible para que el devenir del enfrentamiento sea parecido.

articles.title: “Carlos Has Nothing for Him” – Colby Covington Dismisses Carlos Prates’ Chances Against Islam Makhachev
articles.summary: Colby Covington believes Carlos Prates will be the easiest fight of Islam Makhachev's illustrious UFC career.
articles.body:
It is all but confirmed that Carlos Prates is next in line to challenge Islam Makhachev for the UFC welterweight title. Makhachev defended his belt at UFC 330 against Ian Garry, winning a back-and-forth fight by unanimous decision and extending his UFC winning streak to 17 fights.

However, the fight was far from a walk in the park for the Dagestani. Garry gave Makhachev one of his toughest tests to date , landing some big shots and even opening up the champion. The performance reminded many fans of Makhachev's brutal UFC 284 showdown with Alexander Volkanovski.

Much of the discussion surrounding Makhachev's move to welterweight has centered on the size difference. After spending years at lightweight, the champion is now facing considerably bigger opponents. Many fans believe that could become a major factor against Prates. Colby Covington, however, sees things very differently.

Colby Covington Predicts Islam Makhachev to Submit Carlos Prates in Potential Title Fight

During a recent appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show , Covington shared his thoughts on a potential Makhachev vs. Prates matchup. Rather than expecting a competitive fight, "Chaos" believes Prates could provide the easiest challenge of Makhachev's career.

He said, "Carlos has nothing for him. He's just a straight striker. That's gonna be the easiest fight of Makhachev's career. I think [Makhachev] takes him down and submits him with a kimura or a head-and-arm choke."

Covington did give Prates credit for proving that he can compete over five rounds. However, he believes the Brazilian's smoking habit could become a serious issue when facing someone like Makhachev.

He said, "We know Carlos can go five rounds. He does get a little tired. I mean, it kind of attributes to having a huge, a terrible habit, you know, smoking cigarettes. He needs to quit that if he ever wants to be a legitimate champion."

Helwani also asked Covington about Michael Morales and how he would fare against Makhachev. The Clovis native was less confident in making a prediction, pointing to Morales' limited experience in five-round fights and the need to see how his takedown defense holds up against an elite wrestler.

He said, "We got to see how his [Morales'] takedown defense is. We haven't seen him in any big fights, high-level five-round fights, so we don't know what to expect from him… I think he is still unproven, and there's a lot to be seen from that guy."

With the UFC's 2026 calendar already packed and the remaining numbered events having their main events set, Makhachev's next title defense is likely to happen early in 2027.

Ramadan is expected to begin around February 8, 2027, although the exact date will depend on the sighting of the moon. That could give the UFC a relatively small window to book Makhachev's next title defense, potentially between January and early February.

Getting Makhachev back into the Octagon before Ramadan would also give him a chance to fight twice in 2027. The welterweight champion has generally competed around twice a year in recent seasons, so an early title defense could set him up for another fight in late summer or fall.

Prates, meanwhile, could also benefit from getting back into action soon. The Brazilian has not competed since his May knockout victory over Jack Della Maddalena, leaving him waiting for his next opportunity.

articles.title: Sean Strickland Open to Vacating UFC Middleweight Title
articles.summary: UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland said that he is willing to vacate his title and move up to light heavyweight.Strickland is being targeted for a rem...
articles.body:
UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland said that he is willing to vacate his title and move up to light heavyweight.

Strickland is being targeted for a rematch against rival Nassourdine Imavov, but a public pay dispute has led to this fight not being booked yet.

Things got ugly on Wednesday, when Strickland went to social media to vent about the lowball offer the UFC allegedly made him to fight Imavov.

He even went on to say that he'd be open to giving up his belt and moving up to 205 lbs, as the weight cut is far easier to make light heavyweight for him.

Taking to his social media, Strickland responded to a fan and said that he's open to giving up his belt and moving up in weight.

"Yeah man I wouldnt even care to give up my belt and go to 205. Easier cut…" Strickland wrote on X .

Nassourdine Imavov Confronts Sean Strickland in Las Vegas

In addition to all of his posts going off about low fighter pay, Strickland also got into a skirmish with Team Imavov at the UFC Performance Institute in Las Vegas on Wednesday.

"Imavov: 'What is your problem? You not sign the contract?' Strickland: 'Say what?' Imavov: 'Money? I have money, I give. Hey I'm here, where are you going?'"

What the UFC will do now is the question.

It's clear that Strickland is extremely happy with his UFC fighter pay — he's far from the only fighter to feel like they are underpaid, by the way — and he's even willing to move up in weight and give up his title just to stick it to the UFC .

In addition, it appears that he is open to a boxing match against Jake Paul, a fight that would surely do bonkers numbers on Netflix or whatever other platform carries the bout.

In the end, it's the fans who are losing out, as Strickland is one of the very best MMA fighters in the world, and it's a shame that he isn't getting the chance to show off his skills right now.

articles.title: La IBA creará un nuevo campeonato Mundial con 20 millones de dólares en premios
articles.standfirst: Lo ha anunciado en Estambul, junto a otros proyectos que pueden cambiar y mejorar algunos ámbitos del pugilismo amateur y profesional
articles.summary: Lo ha anunciado en Estambul, junto a otros proyectos que pueden cambiar y mejorar algunos ámbitos del pugilismo amateur y profesional
articles.body: La Asociación Internacional de Boxeo (IBA) ha anunciado en Estambul los principales objetivos de esta organización para los próximos meses, con optimistas proyectos que pueden cambiar y mejorar algunos ámbitos del pugilismo amateur y profesional. Presidieron el acto, el presidente de la IBA, el ruso Umar Kremlev, el secretario general y director ejecutivo, el británico Chris Roberts OBE, y su compatriota, el popular guerrero del peso pesado Derek Chisora, que se niega a retirarse del boxeo profesional. Roberts expuso el sistema que la IBA está desarrollando en torno a sus deportistas. En el centro de este se encuentra IBA Management, que cuenta con un sistema de clasificación único que comenzará con la Copa del Presidente en diciembre. La edición inaugural de la Copa del Presidente de la IBA se celebrará en Estambul del 25 de noviembre al 5 de diciembre, con 12 categorías de peso en juego. Contará con una bolsa de premios de 3 millones de dólares estadounidenses (2,7 millones de euros). Los ganadores recibirán 100.000 dólares (88.800 euros), los medallistas de plata 50.000 y los de bronce 25.000; asimismo, cada victoria obtenida a partir de la ronda inicial reportará al boxeador 1.000 dólares. Está prevista una edición femenina para el próximo año. El torneo sería similar a un Campeonato Mundial en cuanto a tamaño y magnitud, describiéndolo como un evento abierto que sería una verdadera revelación, ya que más de 120 federaciones nacionales ya se han inscrito para el Congreso, a pocas semanas de su celebración. Se cuenta con numerosos patrocinadores y está diseñado para crear las mejores condiciones posibles para atletas y entrenadores. La propia IBA Elite presentará una imagen renovada, con una nueva identidad visual diseñada pensando en un público más joven, que quiere ver una competición intensa y de gran calidad. También se habló de que la IBA organizará su próximo Campeonato Mundial con un fondo de premios de 20 millones de dólares estadounidenses (17,7 millones de euros), de los cuales un millón se otorgará a cada medallista de oro (900.000 euros), según anunció el presidente. El torneo principal de la IBA son los Campeonatos Mundiales. Los Campeonatos Mundiales de Dubái contaron con un premio de 8 millones de dólares estadounidenses y ahora aumenta sensiblemente. Como comentaron en la rueda de prensa, “todo lo que gana la Asociación Internacional de Boxeo pertenece a los entrenadores y atletas, porque gracias a ellos existe nuestra sede internacional del boxeo. Debemos hacer todo lo posible para garantizar las mejores condiciones para nuestros púgiles”. “La nueva directiva es muy positiva y está trabajando para resolver los problemas y las dificultades creadas por la gestión anterior del COI. Esta es una tendencia muy positiva. Sugerimos repetidamente la inclusión de premios en metálico en los Juegos Olímpicos, y finalmente lo implementaron. Una vez más, se demuestra que la IBA tenía razón. El COI siguió nuestro consejo, y nos alegra mucho verlo”, comentó el presidente de la IBA. También dejó claro que la organización está abierta a la cooperación con World Boxing y su presidente, Gennady Golovkin, incluso en la armonización de los calendarios de competición. Los campeones y medallistas olímpicos se clasificarán automáticamente para los Campeonatos Mundiales de la IBA. “Gennady Golovkin es un atleta legendario y le tengo un profundo respeto. No hay ningún conflicto ni desacuerdo. Estamos abiertos a cualquier opción. Diseñaremos nuestro calendario de manera que los atletas tengan la libertad de participar en cualquier evento que deseen”, dijo Kremlev. La creación de nuevos eventos fue otro de los pilares fundamentales de la presentación. Kremlev anunció que en diciembre se celebraría un evento mixto en Miami, combinando combates con puño limpio (Bare Knuckle) y una "Noche de Campeones" de la IBA. Servirá de antesala a cinco torneos de boxeo con puño limpio (Bare Knuckle) de la IBA que se celebrarán en Estados Unidos el próximo año. Por último, Derek Chisora, explicó desde la perspectiva de un boxeador qué es lo que distingue a esta organización. “Imagina que naces en un lugar con condiciones muy difíciles, donde vas al gimnasio y el ring no es estable, y hay solo dos pares de guantes que comparte toda la clase. Kenia, Sudáfrica, Botsuana: todos vienen a Dubái o a Turquía para mostrar sus habilidades. Eso no lo consigues con las promotoras de Londres; ellas solo se centran en los profesionales. Si eres bueno, se fijan más en ti; si no lo eres, no lo hacen. Lo que hace la IBA es increíble: ofrece oportunidades para todos”, comentó el excampeón de Europa. Chisora también aprovechó la conferencia de prensa para anunciar a su próximo rival. “En diciembre me enfrentaré a Murat Gassiev, el campeón mundial WBA del peso pesado. Decidiremos el lugar: Londres o Mánchester”. La idea contó con el respaldo inmediato del presidente de la IBA, quien se mostró dispuesto a apoyar el combate. Por su parte, Chisora, de 42 años, dejó claro que no tiene intención de retirarse del ring. “Nunca dije que me hubiera retirado. Decían que era el ‘último baile’. Pues este es el ‘último baile’ número tres. No tengo nada que demostrar. Simplemente disfruto peleando. Me encanta pelear. Créeme, yo vendo entradas. Ese es mi trabajo”, afirmó entre la sonrisa del público.

articles.title: Diego Lopes explica su salto al peso ligero de la UFC: se enfrentará a Charles Oliveira por el BMF
articles.standfirst: El peleador brasileño no descarta volver a bajar a peso pluma, pero considera que en las 155 libras hay nombres más interesantes de cara a realizar grandes combates
articles.summary: El peleador brasileño no descarta volver a bajar a peso pluma, pero considera que en las 155 libras hay nombres más interesantes de cara a realizar grandes combates
articles.body: Diego Lopes debutará a lo grande en el peso ligero el próximo 12 de diciembre en el combate estelar del UFC 335, donde se enfrentará a Charles Oliveira por el cinturón BMF. A pesar de que a muchos les ha sorprendido este movimiento, el peleador brasileño ha explicado que en peso pluma le quedan pocos retos por realizar ante la falta de nombres interesantes, aunque no descarta volver a bajar en un futuro. Lopes ha vencido a rivales de la talla de Jean Silva, Brian Ortega o Dan Ige, siendo uno de los peleadores más activos y entretenidos de la UFC y ganándose hasta dos oportunidades por el cinturón. Sin embargo, en ambas ocasiones perdió por decisión unánime ante Alexander Volkanovski. Ahora que ve la oportunidad por el cinturón un tanto lejana en esa división, ha decidido afrontar nuevos retos. "Perdí dos veces contra Volk, gané mi última pelea en las 145 libras y ahora mismo no tenemos muchas opciones en esa categoría. Así que decidimos subir a las 155 libras y aceptar algunos combates interesantes", afirmó en una entrevista con Ariel Helwani el peleador brasileño, que ha estado presente en las carteleras históricas de 'La Esfera', el UFC 300 y el UFC Casa Blanca, ganando en todas ellas. Eso sí, Diego no ha descartado volver a bajar a peso pluma, dependiendo de cómo se sienta en esta división. Oliveira es uno de los retos más grandes a los que se puede enfrentar en la categoría, por lo que en caso de dar una buena pelea se demostrará a sí mismo que está preparado para medirse al resto de peces gordos. Sin embargo, en caso de que Movsar Evloev gane a Volkanovski en el UFC 333 y le arrebate el cinturón de peso pluma, se abriría también la puerta a que Diego volviese a bajar de categoría para intentar ser campeón de nuevo y vengar su primera derrota en la UFC. "Ahora puedo hacer más cosas. Puedo tomar suplementos, puedo tomar creatina, puedo levantar más peso. Quiero sentir mi potencia y mi fuerza en las 155 libras y, después de esta pelea, veremos si me quedo o regreso a las 145", finalizó. Lo que está claro es que Lopes y Oliveira protagonizarán un cruce destinado a ser uno de los combates del año. Dos peleadores que van hacia el frente, que tienen buenas habilidades en el suelo y que en el striking no se guardan nada a la hora de buscar la finalización. En caso de ganar, Diego se postularía como una de las grandes estrellas de la UFC poco más de tres años después de su llegada, por lo que habrá mucho en juego.

Those suggesting Osleys Iglesias is the world's best super middleweight boxer can see their man make a case on Thursday night.

Iglesias, a 28-year-old Cuban who stands a shade over 6'2" and has won all 15 of his pro fights (14 by KO) defends the IBF share of the 168-pound throne atop a five-bout main card at the Capitole de Québec theater in Quebec City, Canada.

Osleys Iglesias vs. Oliver Zaren, 12 rounds

Wilkens Mathieu vs. Vladimir Shishkin, 10 rounds

Imam Khataev vs. Padraig McCrory, 10 rounds

Leïla Beaudoin vs. Brisa Abigail Rosario Alfonzo, 10 rounds

Luis Santana vs. Dzmitry Asanau, 10 rounds

Iglesias earned the IBF belt when he stopped Pavel Silyagin in Montreal in April. He's held the lesser-regarded IBO title since his eighth pro fight in 2022 and is ranked second in the weight class by Ring Magazine behind only Canelo Alvarez.

His Danish challenger, Oliver Zaren, is 19-0-1 as a pro and has a win and a draw in two fights in 2026. He's fought in Denmark, Germany, the United Kingdom, and Spain, but this is his first fight trip to North America. He is ranked fifth behind Iglesias by the IBF and 30th by the IBO but is unranked by The Ring

B/R will begin live updates when ring walks begin shortly after 8 p.m.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: The key questions ahead of December 11 all-British showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua
articles.summary: Former world heavyweight champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have a long-running rivalry; They will finally meet in an all-British mega-fight; Fury vs Joshua takes place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff
articles.body:
It is happening. After years of waiting, nursing a rivalry for near enough a decade, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will fight on December 11 at the Principality stadium in Cardiff.

Fury and Joshua, both British heavyweights, both former world champions, have long been linked to fighting. But they held off from actually boxing, unable to come to an agreement. They didn't manage to make the contest for the undisputed crown when they were both reigning champions and then lost their titles to Oleksandr Usyk.

Even the negotiations to finally reach this moment, in the autumn of their respective careers, have been fraught, with Madison Square Garden emerging as a potential venue before the bout was eventually set for the Principality stadium.

The vast resources of Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh has brought this fight together and it was announced that Alalshikh's The Ring and American combat sports promoter Dana White were staging the contest.

However Eddie Hearn, who promotes Joshua, has publicly claimed the American cannot be involved.

But with tickets going on sale on Friday it's inconceivable that promotional wrangling could torpedo the fight. It remains on.

To cater for an international audience, notably in the US, the main event ringwalks are expected to take place at 1am local time with the stadium remaining opening afterwards until 3.30am.

It's been reported that the WBA will put their 'super' heavyweight world championship, the belt vacated by Oleksandr Usyk, on the line even though they already have a 'regular' champion in Murat Gassiev. Sky Sports has contacted the WBA for confirmation.

This has not yet been set. For the time being we can only speculate.

We know that there will be a musical act shortly before the main event, and that it won't be Dua Lipa, but we don't know who it will be.

This is a one-fight deal with no rematch clause in the contract. So a second bout is not guaranteed, but that doesn't mean one can't be negotiated. Public demand for it though will depend on what happens in this first fight.

Well, we'll have a better idea around 1.30am on December 12. Fury and Joshua at their peak offered a fascinating blend of styles. In recent bouts Fury has appeared to be the better preserved of the pair but Joshua has always been a very heavy puncher indeed. There's only one way to find out…

articles.title: Is Sean Strickland fighting Jake Paul? The Tarzan’s UFC contract frustration exploded on social media
articles.summary: Sean Strickland has not booked a fight with Jake Paul, but both men are openly talking about one.
articles.body: Sean Strickland has not booked a fight with Jake Paul, but both men are openly talking about one. On October 7, the UFC middleweight champion posted on X about fighter pay and floated a plan to vacate his belt, move to 205 pounds, finish his UFC contract, and then box Paul. He reclaimed the 185-pound title in May by beating Khamzat Chimaev. Paul replied and pointed him toward his promoter. His title defense against Nassourdine Imavov is still unsigned, and the UFC did not name him on the final numbered card of 2026.Is Sean Strickland really going to fight Jake Paul?Sean Strickland made the idea sound like a real option, and it started with money. He pointed to Conor McGregor's reported $30 million payday and wrote, "they dont want to pay us a fraction of it." He also mentioned a reported $15 million for boxer Conor Benn and called him "Some lame boxer." Benn's signing with Zuffa Boxing had already drawn criticism from MMA fans and fighters.The 185-pound champion would drop the belt he reclaimed in May, go up to 205 pounds and finish the contract fast. Strickland called it "speed running my contract to fight Jake."Paul responded with "If you want your fair share, call MVP when you are free." He also posted a wish list of opponents. McGregor, Canelo Alvarez, Francis Ngannou and Strickland were all on it, along with Tom Aspinall for a boxing match. In another post, Paul asked if Strickland was even out of contract.Strickland expressed his interest for the fight. He wrote, "I haven’t decided if I want to nuke my contract," and added "putting hands on you sounds way better than the UFC right now." Paul's question is the practical hurdle. Strickland has to be free of the UFC before any boxing match.What is going on with the Nassourdine Imavov fight?The pay dispute has already slowed the title fight fans expected next. Last month, Strickland said on X he would face No. 3-ranked Imavov. "Once that detail is squared, it’s locked in," he wrote about the money. He also took a jab at Imavov, writing "no one cares about the fake Frenchman." No announcement has followed, and Strickland has not defended the belt since winning it back.The two crossed paths at the UFC facility in Las Vegas before security separated them. In a clip posted online, Imavov asked, "You not sign the contract?" He then said, "Money? I have money, I give."They have fought before. Strickland won a decision in January 2023. Imavov has not lost since, and he has finished Israel Adesanya and Jared Cannonier along the way.
